name: GridComponent
src_typeComment: The foundation of the Grid Toolkit: drop on an empty GameObject, set width/height/cell size, and you immediately get a visualized grid plus world<->cell conversion — nothing else to wire up. Other grid tools (GridPlacer, GridPathfinder) reference this component rather than duplicating the conversion math.

src_serialized.name: width
src_serialized.tooltip: Number of cells along each axis.

src_serialized.name: plane
src_serialized.tooltip: Which world plane the grid lies on: XZ for a 3D top-down/isometric ground plane, XY for a 2D game.

src_serialized.name: allowDiagonalNeighbors
src_serialized.tooltip: Whether diagonal cells count as neighbors by default (8-directional) or not (4-directional). GetNeighborCells() can still override this per call — GridPathfinder has its own allowDiagonals toggle for exactly that.

src_serialized.name: drawGizmo
src_serialized.tooltip: Draws grid lines in the Scene view.

src_members.sig: public Grid<GameObject> Occupancy { get; private set; }
src_members.name: Occupancy
src_members.comment: Tracks which GameObject (if any) occupies each cell — GridPlacer writes to this, GridPathfinder reads it.

src_members.sig: public Vector3 CellToWorldCenter(int x, int y)
src_members.name: CellToWorldCenter

src_members.sig: public bool WorldToCell(Vector3 worldPosition, out int x, out int y)
src_members.name: WorldToCell
src_members.comment: Returns false (with x/y still populated) if the world position falls outside the grid's bounds.

src_members.sig: public IEnumerable<(int x, int y)> GetNeighborCells(int x, int y) => GetNeighborCells(x, y, allowDiagonalNeighbors)
src_members.name: GetNeighborCells
src_members.comment: Shared adjacency rule for any grid tool that needs neighboring cells (GridPathfinder, or your own range/AoE/flood-fill logic) instead of each one hand-rolling its own 4-vs-8-directional loop. Doesn't filter by walkability/bounds — callers decide what "blocked" or "out of range" means for them.
